Asymmetric MDS by the von Mises model (AMISESCAL)

Source: R/vonmises_mds.R
vonmises_mds.Rd

Each object i is a point x_i in two dimensions with a von Mises distribution of directions, with mean direction mu_i and concentration kappa_i, which expresses toward which direction the object's one-sided relations point (Shojima, 2011, 2012). With theta_ij the direction from x_i to x_j and delta_ij their Euclidean distance, the model for the dissimilarity from i to j is xi_ij = (1 - pi_ij) delta_ij, where pi_ij = c_i exp{kappa_i (cos(theta_ij - mu_i) - 1)}. pi_ij is the von Mises density omega_i exp{kappa_i cos(theta - mu_i)} / I0(kappa_i) of Shojima (2012) rewritten with its peak c_i = omega_i exp(kappa_i) / I0(kappa_i); c_i < 1 keeps pi_ij < 1. An object j lying in the direction mu_i looks closer from i than i looks from j.

Usage

vonmises_mds(
  x,
  type = c("dissimilarity", "similarity"),
  omega = c("free", "fixed"),
  prior = list(),
  nrandom = 10,
  maxit = 2000,
  reltol = 1e-10,
  hessian = FALSE,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

x

A square matrix of asymmetric proximities. Rows evaluate columns (x[i, j] is from i to j). The diagonal is ignored; other missing cells are left out of the fit.

type

"dissimilarity" (default) or "similarity". Similarities are reversed as max + min - x. If x has a type attribute set by as_proximity(), that is used.

omega

"free" (default; Shojima, 2012) or "fixed" (1 / (2 pi); Shojima, 2011). See Details.

prior

A list with x_sd, kappa_shape, kappa_rate, c_a and c_b. See Details. Missing elements take the defaults list(x_sd = 1, kappa_shape = 2, kappa_rate = 0.5, c_a = 2, c_b = 4).

nrandom

Number of random starts in addition to the rational start.

maxit, reltol

Passed to stats::optim().

hessian

Logical; compute approximate standard errors.

seed

Random seed for the random starts. The state of the random number generator is restored afterwards. NULL uses (and advances) the current state.

Value

An object of class c("mdspace_vonmises", "mdspace") with conf (n x 2, in units of the scaled dissimilarities), mu (radians), kappa, c (peaks of pi), sigma, stress (sqrt(sum((g - xi)^2) / sum(g^2)) on the scaled dissimilarities), logpost (log posterior at the mode, up to a constant), niter, pi and xi (n x n; xi in the original units), scale (the root mean square used for scaling), anchor (labels of the three anchors), starts (logpost of each start, the rational one first), best_start, converged, and with hessian = TRUE, se (a data frame of standard errors of mu, kappa and c).

Details

With omega = "fixed" the density is the ordinary von Mises density (omega_i = 1 / (2 pi), Shojima, 2011), so that c_i is determined by kappa_i, and kappa_i < 6.5 keeps c_i < 1. With omega = "free" (Shojima, 2012) c_i is a parameter of its own. Leaving it free without further constraint lets the solution degenerate (points move apart while all pi_ij approach 1), which the original program prevents by an additional term in the stress function. Here the estimates are instead the mode of a posterior distribution (maximum a posteriori, MAP) with weak priors, the same as the Bayesian version written in Stan (develop/vonmises_mds.stan in the source repository): g_ij ~ N(xi_ij, sigma^2), deviations of the coordinates from their centroid ~ N(0, prior$x_sd^2), kappa_i ~ Gamma(prior$kappa_shape, prior$kappa_rate) truncated at the upper bound, c_i ~ Beta(prior$c_a, prior$c_b) and sigma ~ half-t(4, 0, 1). The dissimilarities are divided by their root mean square before fitting, so that the priors are on a common scale.

The configuration is identified as in the Bayesian version by a Cholesky factor (lower triangular with positive diagonal; Stan Development Team, Reference Manual, "Cholesky factors of covariance matrices"): one anchor object is placed at the origin, the second on the positive side of the first axis and the third on the positive side of the second axis. The anchors are chosen from the Torgerson solution of the symmetric part so that they are far apart and not on a line. This anchoring is only a device for computation: the likelihood and the prior (placed on the deviations from the centroid, which is isotropic) do not change under translation, rotation and reflection, so the solution does not depend on which objects are the anchors. The mean directions rotate with the configuration, so they are identified too. For presentation the returned configuration is centered and rotated to its principal axes, and the mean directions are rotated with it.

The posterior mode has many local optima, so the rational start (the Torgerson solution with each mean direction pointing at the objects toward which the object has one-sided relations) and nrandom random starts are tried and the best is returned. The minimization uses the analytic gradient and stats::optim() (BFGS). With hessian = TRUE approximate standard errors of mu, kappa and c are obtained from the Hessian of the negative log posterior (Laplace approximation; delta method for the transformed parameters).

References

Shojima, K. (2011). Asymmetric von Mises scaling. Proceedings of the 39th Annual Meeting of the Behaviormetric Society of Japan, 261-262.

Shojima, K. (2012). On the stress function of asymmetric von Mises scaling. Paper presented at the Joint Meeting of the German Classification Society and the Japanese Classification Society.

Mardia, K. V., & Jupp, P. E. (2000). Directional statistics. Wiley.

Stan Development Team. Stan reference manual: Cholesky factors of covariance matrices. https://mc-stan.org/docs/reference-manual/

Examples

x <- matrix(c(NA, 5, 4, 5, 3,
              6, NA, 4, 2, 1,
              4, 4, NA, 3, 3,
              4, 1, 2, NA, 1,
              7, 1, 2, 1, NA), 5, byrow = TRUE,
            dimnames = list(LETTERS[1:5], LETTERS[1:5]))
fit <- vonmises_mds(x, nrandom = 2)
fit
